crosswalk. pedestrian-torres stated he saw him coming and turned his shoulder so it would not hit his body. pedestrian-torres stated the right mirror from the red [identifier] truck (unit #1) hit his left shoulder and the mirror bent in wards. pedestrian-torres stated the student looked at him and drove off. pedestrian-torres stated he then went to the principals office to report the incident. the responding officer asked pedestrian-torres if he knew the student who was driving or his name. pedestrian-torres stated he did not know him or his name. i asked pedestrian-torres if there were any credible witnesses that had seen the incident. pedestrian-torres stated just a girl that was behind him but he does not know her or her name. i asked pedestrian- torres how he felt when the mirror from the truck struck him in the shoulder. pedestrian-torres stated at first, he didnt feel much but then a few minutes later his arm began to hurt. pedestrian-torres advised a 5 out of 10 scale of pain, to left his arm. pedestrian-torres stated the campus nurse gave him ice to put his arm. pedestrian-torres provided the plates of the red in color [identifier] truck, tx-plates [identifier]. the mother of pedestrian-torres stated she was going to take her son pedestrian-torres to the urgent care for further treatment. in the investigation, officer met with the assistant [school facility] in her office in reference to this case. quinn stated in her administration investigation she was able to positively identify the driver of the red [identifier] ford truck (unit #1) as student a. d. quinn stated she had conducted an interview with student a. d on the incident. quinn stated student a. d told her that he drives a red [identifier] ford truck (unit #1) [school facility] and that he leaves campus because he picks up his brother and sister. quinn stated student a. d told her that the student was jogging and bumped into his truck. quinn stated student a. d told her that the student got mad and pushed in his side mirror. quinn stated student a. d provided an administration statement on the incident. driver of unit #1 information was updated on the collision report. the responding officer reviewed the security surveillance video footage for the franklin magnet center (franklin hs ch1 november 15, 2024 at 02:30:24 pm to 02:30:47 pm) which revealed a red in color [identifier] truck (unit #1) stopped in front of the crosswalk in the student parking lot. a large number of students can be seen crossing the crosswalk in front of the truck. after several students crossed the crosswalk, simultaneously, unit #1 can be seen moving forward slowly into the crosswalk and pedestrian-torres walking at the beginning of the crosswalk walking towards the front right side of unit #1. unit #1 can be seen crossing the crosswalk slowly and then pedestrian-torres continued to walk towards the right side of unit #1 inside the crosswalk. pedestrian-torres can be seen continuing to walk next to the side and the back of the truck as it passed in front of him. pedestrian-torres can be seen walking normally toward the campus. the video footage does not show any contact being made to pedestrian-torres due to the angle of the camera. the investigation revealed, the driver of unit #1 and pedestrian-torres had inconsistent statements as to how the collision or contact occurred, in which there is not enough of substantial evidence to determine who was at fault, as unit #1 proceed into the middle of the crosswalk, and pedestrian-torres continued to proceed into the crosswalk in the path of a vehicle so close that it is impossible for the vehicle to operator to stop or yield. the video footage does not show any contact being made to pedestrian-torres due to the angle of the camera. there was no credible witness at the scene. no citation was issued. this case will be inactive.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was traveling west through the family dollar parking lot when the driver attempted to maneuver into a parking space located next to the sidewalk in front of the store. the driver accelerated and drove unit 1 onto the sidewalk, colliding into an ice machine positioned outside the establishment. the force of the impact propelled the ice machine into mary zapata, who was standing nearby, resulting in a violent collision that caused her to be knocked over, ultimately landing near the entrance of the family dollar store. after the collision, the driver of unit 1 reversed the vehicle and returned to the parking space where he had originally attempted to park. as a result of the impact with the ice machine, unit 1 sustained front-end damage, as well as left-side damage from sideswiping the building. zapata sustained serious injuries as a result of the [medical facility] for medical attention. during an interview with the driver, he detailed that he had been accompanied by his sister throughout the morning, who assisted him with a pedicure to address his ongoing foot conditions. he recounted a specific moment when he felt his foot become ""hung,"" which led to the vehicle accelerating onto the sidewalk. the driver also noted that his legs do not function very well and revealed that he has titanium plates in his right leg. when his sister arrived at the scene, she corroborated the drivers account of their morning together and emphasized the extensive treatment she had provided, including surgeries on both of his feet. she elaborated on the severity of his foot issues. during an interview with zapata, she mentioned looking at the clearance rack outside the family dollar store. suddenly, she found herself on the ground and could hardly remember what had happened.

tires on the right side of #5. unit 4 had hazard lights activated. unit 4 was parked next to the fog line and the back left corner of unit 5 [roadway]. the back left corner of #5 was measured and it was approximately one foot into the outside, [roadway] from the fog line. the hay bales extended approximately three additional inches from [roadway]. the driver of unit 6 had come to the scene to assist with the tire changing. unit 6 was parked in the southbound drainage ditch on the right side of #4 and #5, facing south. the driver of #3 had also stopped at the scene to assist with the tire changing. unit 3 parked facing traffic on the southbound side of the [roadway] that was just north of #5. unit 3 had its lights on (98). due to it becoming nighttime and the lights from #3 shining brightly toward oncoming, southbound traffic as they crested a hill, this impaired the vision of southbound traffic. unit 7 was a pedestrian, who saw what was going on and [roadway] where unit 3 had parked, belonged to #7's residence. unit 1 was towing unit 2 and was traveling [roadway]. as #1 crested the hill, the lights from #3 were shining in into the eyes of the driver. #1 driver was unable to see what was going on. this caused #1 driver steer toward the southbound improved shoulder. this movement resulted in the front right of #2 striking the front right of #3. as #1 and #2 continued southbound, the front right of #1 struck the back left of #5 and the hay bale. the collision with #5 caused multiple hay bales to fall over onto the right side of the trailer, where multiple people were changing the flat tires. one hay bale fell onto unit 6, causing top damage. another hay bale struck #7, causing minor injuries. #1 and #2 continued southbound, where it side swiped #4. #1 skidded out of control into the southbound traffic lanes. #1 spun clockwise, causing #1 and #2 to go into a jackknife position. the front right of #2 struck the right side of #1. unit 1 came to rest facing southwest with severe front right damage and moderate right side damage. unit 2 came to rest still attached to #1, facing south with moderate front right damage. witness statements were collected advising that it was difficult to see due unit 3's head lights shining toward southbound traffic. there was also dash camera footage obtained from a motorist that was not involved in the crash. the footage does not capture the collision, but it did show what was occurring prior to the collision. the vehicle that had the dash camera was driving in front of unit 1. the collision happened shortly after this vehicle had driven past all the stopped units. the video footage showed the lights from #3 were extremely bright.

records.public_safe_text: unit 4, towing unit 5 (a utility trailer loaded with multiple round hay bales), was stopped facing, southbound on us 281 as the driver of #4 was dealing with two flat tires on the right side of #5. unit 4 had hazard lights activated. unit 4 was parked next to the fog line and the back left corner of unit 5 [roadway]. the back left corner of #5 was measured and it was approximately one foot into the outside, [roadway] from the fog line. the hay bales extended approximately three additional inches from [roadway]. the driver of unit 6 had come to the scene to assist with the tire changing. unit 6 was parked in the southbound drainage ditch on the right side of #4 and #5, facing south. the driver of #3 had also stopped at the scene to assist with the tire changing. unit 3 parked facing traffic on the southbound side of the [roadway] that was just north of #5. unit 3 had its lights on (98). due to it becoming nighttime and the lights from #3 shining brightly toward oncoming, southbound traffic as they crested a hill, this impaired the vision of southbound traffic. unit 7 was a pedestrian, who saw what was going on and [roadway] where unit 3 had parked, belonged to #7's residence. unit 1 was towing unit 2 and was traveling [roadway]. as #1 crested the hill, the lights from #3 were shining in into the eyes of the driver. #1 driver was unable to see what was going on. this caused #1 driver steer toward the southbound improved shoulder. this movement resulted in the front right of #2 striking the front right of #3. as #1 and #2 continued southbound, the front right of #1 struck the back left of #5 and the hay bale. the collision with #5 caused multiple hay bales to fall over onto the right side of the trailer, where multiple people were changing the flat tires. one hay bale fell onto unit 6, causing top damage. another hay bale struck #7, causing minor injuries. #1 and #2 continued southbound, where it side swiped #4. #1 skidded out of control into the southbound traffic lanes. #1 spun clockwise, causing #1 and #2 to go into a jackknife position. the front right of #2 struck the right side of #1. unit 1 came to rest facing southwest with severe front right damage and moderate right side damage. unit 2 came to rest still attached to #1, facing south with moderate front right damage. witness statements were collected advising that it was difficult to see due unit 3's head lights shining toward southbound traffic. there was also dash camera footage obtained from a motorist that was not involved in the crash. the footage does not capture the collision, but it did show what was occurring prior to the collision. the vehicle that had the dash camera was driving in front of unit 1. the collision happened shortly after this vehicle had driven past all the stopped units. the video footage showed the lights from #3 were extremely bright.

frame. i did observe broken glass, spider web, to the bottom right side of the front windshield (passenger side). isaac, who was traveling directly behind unit 1, gave a similar recollection of events observed the area to be wet from the ongoing rain and visibility was slightly darker even with the lights provided by the parking lot and store due to the rain. the pedestrian was transported to medical city lewisville by hvfd medical unit [identifier].

records.public_safe_text: on [date] at 1824 hours, officers were dispatched as well as highland village medics to (wal-mart) [roadway]., highland village, denton county, texas 75077 in reference to an mvc-inj with a vehicle vs. pedestrian in front of the grocery side entrance. upon arrival, officers observed the pedestrian that was hit by unit# 1 sitting on the ground approximately 1 foot from unit# 1 with a paper towel in her hand to wipe any blood from her head wound. officers made contact with the driver of unit# 1 who stated she was heading towards the [roadway] when she stopped to let people walk from the store to the parking spaces. the driver of unit# 1 stated she began to pull forward when all of a sudden she hit the pedestrian walking towards the grocery side entrance doors. the driver of unit# 1 stated she didn't see the pedestrian. officer made contact with a witness #1 steve ceranowicz ([phone]) who was volunteering for salvation army outside the grocery side entrance doors just 10 to 15 feet from the accident. witness #1 stated he couldn't see the pedestrian until unit# 1 hit her due to the dark clothing she was wearing along with the rainy weather. witness #1 stated unit #1 hit the pedestrian with the driver side corner of the front bumper hitting the pedestrians right leg causing her to fall on the hood and then to the ground. officers made contact with witness #2 ivy forbey ([phone]) who stated as she was about to walk into the grocery side entrance door she heard a noise and turned around to see the pedestrian fall from the hood of unit# 1 to the ground. officers made contact with the pedestrian who stated she was walking towards the grocery side entrance and all of a sudden was hit by unit# 1 and fell hitting her head. officers observed the area to be wet from the ongoing rain and visibility was slightly darker even with the lights provided by the parking lot and store due to the rain. the pedestrian was transported to medical city lewisville by hvfd medical unit [identifier].
